rationale: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible but unsupported by key empirical data and requires targeted de-risking before adoption. Critical evidence gaps include: (1) in vivo validation that the exogenous spike-in faithfully models endogenous EV biodistribution and membrane-protection in the intended species/matrices; (2) demonstration that immuno-capture + particle-count orthogonal assays have sufficient sensitivity/specificity in short-interval nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-adjacent tissue; and (3) timing/kinetic data showing intact-EV presence in sampled compartments. Substantial CMC/scale-up and stability risks (reproducible production of capture-positive vs capture-depleted fractions, lot comparability) further necessitate process studies. Recommend spike-in behavior validation, orthogonal assay sensitivity experiments in the target species/matrices, and small-scale manufacturing comparability/stability studies prior to progressing to in vivo efficacy/potency testing.
